title: A positive feedback loop between KPNA2 and FOXM1 promotes the proliferation of lung adenocarcinoma.
authors: Wang, Ying; Jin, Yan; Li, Xin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究KPNA2与转录因子FOXM1的正反馈环路促进肺腺癌增殖，虽涉及FOXM1-DNA结合（ChIP）和AlphaFold3蛋白互作预测，但核心是肿瘤生物学而非TF-DNA互作机制建模，方法上仅简单使用AlphaFold3，缺乏AI/物理模拟深度。
abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma is a prevalent form of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that accounts for approximately 40% of all lung cancers. However, despite significant therapeutic advances in recent years, the overall survival of patients with lung adenocarcinoma remains poor. Consequently, it is necessary to identify further novel targets and drugs that can contribute to enhancing the prognosis of these patients. To this end, in this study, using siRNA silencing, we initially knocked down KPNA2 in lung adenocarcinoma cell lines, and performed CCK8 and 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine assays to examine the proliferation of lung adenocarcinoma. Chromatin immunoprecipitation was used to determine whether the transcription factor FOXM1 can bind to the promoter region of KPNA2, and we used AlphaFold3 to predict the proteins that bind to KPNA2 and to characterize the binding sites on these proteins. We found that KPNA2 is upregulated in lung adenocarcinoma and that inhibiting its expression effectively reduced the proliferation of lung adenocarcinoma cancer cells. Both bioinformatics analyses and experimental findings provided evidence that the expression of KPNA2 is directly controlled by FOXM1. Furthermore, we observed a reduction in FOXM1 expression following the suppression of KPNA2. These findings indicate the presence of a positive feedback loop between the expression of KPNA2 and FOXM1, which contributes to an enhanced proliferation of lung adenocarcinoma cells.
abstract_zh: 肺腺癌是非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）的一种常见形式，约占所有肺癌的40%。然而，尽管近年来治疗取得了显著进展，肺腺癌患者的总体生存率仍然较低。因此，有必要进一步识别新的靶点和药物，以有助于改善这些患者的预后。为此，在本研究中，我们首先通过siRNA沉默技术敲低肺腺癌细胞系中的KPNA2，并进行了CCK8和5-乙炔基-2'-脱氧尿苷实验以检测肺腺癌的增殖情况。使用染色质免疫沉淀技术来确定转录因子FOXM1是否能与KPNA2的启动子区域结合，并利用AlphaFold3预测与KPNA2结合的蛋白质及其结合位点特征。我们发现KPNA2在肺腺癌中表达上调，抑制其表达能有效降低肺腺癌癌细胞的增殖。生物信息学分析和实验证据均表明，KPNA2的表达受FOXM1直接调控。此外，我们观察到在抑制KPNA2后，FOXM1的表达也有所下降。这些发现表明，KPNA2与FOXM1的表达之间存在正反馈环路，这有助于增强肺腺癌细胞的增殖。
